messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 decode latency spike detected in us-west-2 serving pool. Alert ID INCIDENT-2024-1755554321. p99 increased from ~250ms -> ~2.1s. Affected route: /v1/generate (streaming). Paging on-call.

emma: ack — I'm looking at traces and top hosts. grabbing flamegraphs.

raj: oncall here, will pull perf events and recent kernel/runtime deploy history.

sre_lead: tagging @alex and eng-runtime for possible compile/runtime regression.

alex: looking at deploys — runtime image redwood/runtime:1755520000 pushed ~6h ago with new TRT/FlashAttention kernels and compile flags `--enable-compiler-flashopt`. Also saw a tiny kernel tweak in the compilepath container.

maria: CS: a few customers reported streaming stalls and elevated tail latency. One enterprise tenant saw ~20% of requests with timeouts. Notified account teams.

emma: logs look like repeated kernel page reclaim / eviction around the time of spikes. snippet from node-3 dmesg:

```
[12345.678901] kernel: kswapd0: page allocation failure, order:0
[12345.678905] decode: GPU kernel queued but stalled on page fault at 0x7ffabcd1234
[12345.678910] audit: MMAP fault in process decode_worker pid=2245
```

raj: perf sampling shows decode threads spending long time in `do_page_fault`/`mm_fault` on affected nodes. KV cache hit rates unchanged. looks like on-demand eviction + new kernel interplay.

oncall-bot: Note: Autoscaler backlog > 0 and pool can't scale due to soft quota. New nodes blocked — may be amplifying tail effects.

alex: I suspect the new FlashAttention/TRT kernel introduces different memory access patterns that increase page churn under certain batch sizes. Proposal: quick rollback to previous runtime image and enable reference kernel fallback for streaming routes.

emma: quick mitigation steps applied: reduced default batch size -> 1 for streaming svc and set env fallback `REDWOOD_USE_REF_KERNEL=1` on streaming-svc in prod.

Command run:
```
kubectl set env deploy/streaming-svc REDWOOD_USE_REF_KERNEL=1 -n prod
kubectl patch deploy/streaming-svc -n prod -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"svc","env":[{"name":"DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE","value":"1"}]}]}}}}'
```

maria: drafting customer update now: "Temporary mitigations applied (fallback kernel + batch size reduction). Root cause under investigation. We will follow up with timeline and postmortem."

sre_lead: we should also roll back the compile flag `--enable-compiler-flashopt` and the runtime image. Alex, can you coordinate? We'll do a 10% canary then monitor p99/p95.

alex: initiating canary rollback via deploy-bot: `/deploy streaming-svc --image=redwood/runtime:1755508000 --canary=10%`

deploy-bot: started canary deployment (10% traffic) for streaming-svc image:redwood/runtime:1755508000

emma: canary p99 shows improvement on canary nodes: 2.1s -> ~1.1s. still above normal but better.

raj: digging into kernel counters — when canary traffic hits old image, page-fault latencies drop and decode kernel wait times vanish. I think the compilepath + flash kernel changes increased working set pressure and caused more frequent evictions.

emma: enabling temporary KV pin on canary nodes to reduce eviction churn: `REDWOOD_KV_PIN=1`

alex: starting 100% rollout if canary continues to improve. owner: me for rollback.

deploy-bot: canary healthy, proceeding to 100% rollout for streaming-svc image:redwood/runtime:1755508000

emma: watching metrics — cluster-wide p99 trending down. current p99 ~220ms, p95 ~90ms.

raj: collecting flamegraphs + perf dumps and uploading artifacts to internal incident bucket: `/internal/incidents/1755554321/traces.tar.gz`

maria: CS update sent: customers notified mitigations and that we're rolling back runtime image as a temporary fix.

sre_lead: good. incident status: mitigation in progress. once cluster p99 stable for 30m, we'll mark resolved and handoff to eng-runtime for full postmortem. Owners: @alex (rollback), @raj (traces), @emma (monitoring), @maria (customer comms).

deploy-bot: rollout 100% completed.

emma: cluster p99 back to ~220ms across us-west-2. streaming errors dropped to baseline. I'll keep an eye for 30m and then handoff.

raj: saved counters and config: kernel config, gcc/clang compile flags, TRT/FlashAttention kernel versions. Will attach to postmortem.

maria: confirming affected customer loops closed.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT-2024-1755554321 RESOLVED at 2024-05-15T15:47:00Z. Follow-up required: postmortem + label `kernel-compile-regression`.

sre_lead: thanks team. let's schedule a blameless postmortem, include reproduction steps, perf diffs, and test a controlled re-introduction of the FlashAttention changes behind feature flags and with memory pressure tests.

alex: will own rollback PR + controlled re-roll plan. raj and emma, please add your artifacts to the ticket.

emma: noted, will dump dashboards and alerts to incident ticket.

maria: closing customer communications loop.
